# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-run) throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches; the legacy system remains fully operational and authoritative for unmigrated users until all phases complete and a separate post-migration validation period has passed.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — ~2,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, tax calculation, and refund flows, with zero critical defects open, and a rollback procedure has been tested successfully at least once.

- Cohort: Internal accounts, employee accounts, and opted-in low-risk customers (e.g., monthly plans under a defined spend threshold, no active disputes).
- Both systems run in parallel; new system is authoritative for migrated users, old system retains a synced read-only copy for reconciliation.
- Duration: minimum 2 weeks or until 3 consecutive billing cycles complete cleanly for the pilot cohort.

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout (35% of users — ~14,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit metrics met (see Metrics section) for two consecutive full billing cycles, support ticket volume attributable to migration is below 1% of migrated users, and finance has reconciled Phase 1 invoicing totals against the legacy system with less than 0.1% variance.

- Cohort: Broader mix of plan types and geographies, excluding highest-value enterprise accounts and known edge cases (multi-entity billing, custom contracts).
- Migration executed in sub-waves of ~2,000–3,000 users per week to preserve ability to pause between waves.
- Customer support and finance teams are staffed for elevated ticket volume during this phase.

## Phase 3: General Availability / Full Migration (60% of users — ~24,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit metrics met for two consecutive billing cycles, all known edge-case billing scenarios (proration, multi-currency, enterprise contracts) have been validated against the new system with real or shadow transactions, and executive sign-off obtained from Finance and Customer Success.

- Cohort: All remaining users, including highest-value and highest-complexity accounts, migrated last and in smaller, closely monitored sub-batches.
- Old billing system remains active in parallel (read/write standby, not decommissioned) through this phase and through a subsequent stabilization period.
- Legacy system decommissioning is explicitly out of scope for Phase 3 and will be addressed only in a separate, later Phase 4 (Legacy Decommission) after a minimum 60-day stabilization window with no P1/P2 billing incidents.

---

## Metrics and Halt Conditions
- **Halt the rollout immediately if failed/erroneous payment transactions among migrated users exceed 0.5% of migrated transactions in any 24-hour window.**
- Halt or pause a batch if billing discrepancy (amount charged vs. amount expected) affects more than 25 accounts in a single sub-wave.
- Halt if customer-reported billing support tickets exceed 3% of the currently migrated user base within a 48-hour period.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of customers during dual-run period | Implement idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that cross-checks both systems daily before settlement | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors (e.g., incorrect plan, tax, or currency mapping) causing incorrect invoices | Run shadow billing (parallel invoice generation without charging) for each cohort for one full cycle before cutover | Data Migration Team Lead
RISK: Customer support overwhelmed by migration-related inquiries | Pre-stage FAQs, train support staff before each phase, and scale on-call support capacity proportional to phase size | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Legacy system dependency (e.g., third-party integrations, tax engine) not fully replicated in new system | Conduct integration parity audit and require sign-off from Integrations team before Phase 2 entry | Integrations Engineering Lead
RISK: Rollback becomes impractical after large batches migrate due to state drift between systems | Cap batch sizes and require successful rollback drill before each phase, keep legacy system as source of truth until final validation | Platform Reliability Owner

PHASES: 3
